tower-of-hanoi.title: Identify already-correct disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Compare the initial configuration with the goal configuration to find disks that already sit on their final peg and already have the correct relative order beneath them. Those disks can be treated as fixed and need not be moved again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, before planning any moves, or after a series of moves when re‑evaluating the state.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If the goal requires disk 5 on peg 2 and disk 5 is already on peg 2 with no smaller disks beneath it, you can leave it untouched.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Determine descending placement order
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The final stack on the goal peg must be built from largest to smallest; therefore plan to place disks in strictly decreasing size, ensuring each new disk is smaller than the current top of the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the sequence of moves that builds the goal stack, especially after identifying which disks are already correct.
tower-of-hanoi.example: For a goal of [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, move disk 5 first, then 4, then 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate every smaller disk that lies above it, using an auxiliary peg, before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a target larger disk is buried under smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 4 from peg 0 that has disks 2 and 1 on top, first move 1 and 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use auxiliary peg for temporary storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When clearing blocking disks, place them on the peg that is neither the source peg of the larger disk nor the intended destination peg, thereby keeping the path clear and preserving the ability to later retrieve them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the clearing step for a larger disk, after identifying which peg is free of both source and destination.
tower-of-hanoi.example: While moving disk 4 from peg 0 to peg 2, move disks 1 and 2 to peg 1 (the auxiliary peg).

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid premature placement on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a smaller disk onto the goal peg until all larger disks that must end up below it have already been placed there; otherwise the smaller disk would block the required larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever considering moving a disk to the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not move disk 1 to the goal peg before disks 5, 4, and 3 have been placed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Re‑stack displaced smaller disks after larger ones
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After a larger disk has been moved to its final position on the goal peg, retrieve any smaller disks that were temporarily moved away and place them back onto the goal peg in the correct descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Immediately after completing the placement of a larger disk and before moving to the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 4 onto the goal peg, move disks 2 and 1 (which were on the auxiliary peg) onto the goal peg, respecting order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track top disks and legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date mental or written representation of the topmost disk on each peg, and before each move verify that the moving disk is the topmost and that the destination peg’s top disk (if any) is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before executing any move in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If peg 0’s top is disk 1, you cannot move disk 2 from peg 0 until disk 1 has been moved elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate and verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the full move list, replay the moves from the initial state to ensure every move is legal and that the final configuration exactly matches the goal; this catches errors before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the complete move sequence, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run through the moves step‑by‑step on paper or mentally and confirm the final stack on peg 2 is [5,4,3,2,1].

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move decomposition
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a transfer of n disks by recursively moving the top n‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the n‑th (largest) disk to the destination, then recursively moving the n‑1 disks from the auxiliary peg onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the problem reduces to moving a contiguous stack of disks from one peg to another, especially after clearing steps have isolated such a sub‑stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg A to peg C using B as auxiliary: first move disks 1‑2 to B, then move disk 3 to C, then move disks 1‑2 from B to C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat larger base disks on destination as fixed
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg already contains a disk that is larger than all disks you intend to place onto it, you can treat that larger disk as a fixed base and safely build the remaining stack on top of it without moving it again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal peg already has a large disk (e.g., the largest disk) that will remain at the bottom of the final stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 to an empty peg 2, you can treat it as a fixed base and subsequently place disks 4, 3, 2, 1 on top.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving a desired disk without checking the size of the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always compare the sizes of the moving disk and the destination peg’s top disk; only move if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget that only the top disk can be moved, especially when multiple disks are stacked.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a record of the current top disk on each peg and verify that the chosen disk matches that top before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Temporarily placing a small disk on the goal peg before a larger disk that must be below it
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may aim to reduce moves by placing a small disk early, overlooking the final order requirement.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the rule that a smaller disk may only be placed on the goal peg after all larger disks that belong below it have been placed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Leaving blocking disks on the target peg when moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a larger disk onto a peg without first clearing smaller disks that sit on that peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg, ensure the peg’s top disk (if any) is larger; otherwise relocate the smaller blocking disks to the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Failing to verify that the final configuration matches the goal
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the sequence is correct without checking the end state.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After constructing the move list, replay the moves from the initial state and compare the resulting configuration with the goal.
